examples.knowledge_point: Solving Rational Equations Containing Two Distinct Linear Denominators
examples.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

Now, let's multiply both sides of the equation by the least common denominator. The equation has the denominators $8x$ and $2x,$ so the least common multiple (or $\textrm{LCM}$) of the denominators is

$$
\textrm{LCM}(8x,2x) = 8x.
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $8x$ and simplifying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3-\frac{10x+7}{8x} & =\frac{6x-3}{2x} \\ 8x\cdot (3-\frac{10x+7}{8x}) & =8x\cdot (\frac{6x-3}{2x}) \\ 8x\cdot 3-8x\cdot (\frac{10x+7}{8x}) & =8x\cdot (\frac{6x-3}{2x}) \\ 24x-\cancel{8x}\cdot (\frac{10x+7}{\cancel{8x}}) & =4\cdot \cancel{2x}\cdot (\frac{6x-3}{\cancel{2x}}) \\ 24x-(10x+7) & =4\cdot (6x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $x,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}24x-(10x+7) & =4\cdot (6x-3) \\ 14x-7 & =24x-12 \\ 24x-14x & =-7+12 \\ 10x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall that we cannot allow $x=0$ as a solution. Since $x= \dfrac 12$ is different from $x=0,$ we accept it as a solution. 

Therefore, the solution is $x= \dfrac 12.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that $z=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by $2z,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z+1}{2z} & =2-\frac{2z+1}{2z} \\ 2z\cdot (\frac{z+1}{2z}) & =2z\cdot (2-\frac{2z+1}{2z}) \\ 2z\cdot \frac{z+1}{2z} & =2z\cdot 2-2z\cdot \frac{2z+1}{2z} \\ \cancel{2z}\cdot \frac{z+1}{\cancel{2z}} & =2z\cdot 2-\cancel{2z}\cdot \frac{2z+1}{\cancel{2z}} \\ z+1 & =4z-(2z+1) \\ z+1 & =4z-2z-1\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $z,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+1 & =4z-2z-1 \\ z+1 & =2z-1 \\ -z & =-2 \\ z & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $z=0$ as a solution. But since $z=2\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $z=2.$
